spotatui
 
 
 A fast music player for the terminal and the desktop, written in Rust. 
 Spotify through its own built-in client, plus local files, Subsonic/Navidrome, internet radio, YouTube and Qobuz, and Apple Music on macOS.
 
 
 Download · Install · Docs · Contributing · Discord 
 

 
 
 
 
 

 Desktop app 

 

 Terminal app 

 

 
 
 Table of Contents

- About
- Installation
- Quickstart
- Sources
- Learn more
- Contributing
- Song History
- Star History
- Maintainers
- Code signing policy
- spotatui Contributors

 

 About

spotatui is a music player with two frontends: a desktop app and a terminal app. They share one login, one configuration and one listening history. Spotify is optional: it is one of seven sources.

- Synced lyrics, and a real-time audio visualizer.
- A play queue that mixes tracks from different sources.
- Playlist sync: mirror one playlist onto Spotify, Qobuz, Subsonic or YouTube.
- Lua plugins for commands, keys, popups and themes.
- An AI DJ inside the app, or your coding agent as the DJ over MCP.
- A local listening history with stats and a shareable recap.
- A CLI for playback, search and playlists.

 Spotify needs Premium. spotatui logs in with its own built-in client, so you need no developer app and no client ID.

spotatui started as a fork of spotify-tui and has since grown its own player, sources and desktop app.

 Installation

Spotify is optional: every other source works without an account.

 Desktop app 

 System Download 
 --- --- 
 Windows 10/11 Installer 
 macOS Apple Silicon · Intel 
 Linux .deb · .rpm · AppImage 

The installers are not signed yet, so Windows and macOS warn on the first start. Desktop app shows how to open it, and lists the arm64 files for Linux.

 Terminal app 

 System Command 
 --- --- 
 macOS, Linux, WSL curl -fsSL \ bash 
 Windows irm \ iex or winget install spotatui 
 Arch Linux yay -S spotatui-bin 
 With Rust cargo install --locked spotatui 

Homebrew, Nix, Void, .deb packages and building from source are in the installation guide.

- Features per build: the prebuilt terminal binaries include every source, the MCP server and the AI DJ. cargo install builds Spotify only unless you add the features, and the Nix flake builds Spotify only.
- Updates: the terminal app updates itself. If a package manager installed it, set behavior.disable auto update: true . See Updating.

 Quickstart

Run spotatui . The first launch asks which sources you want. Pick Spotify to log in: spotatui shows a code and opens Spotify's pairing page, where you confirm it.

Then:

- ? lists every key.
- / searches. Choose the Songs panel with the arrow keys, press Enter to go into it, and Enter again to play a track.
- d switches the source and the device.
- z queues a track, and Shift+Q opens the queue.
- spotatui --help shows the CLI.

 Sources

 Source You need 
 --- --- 
 Spotify A Premium account 
 Local Files A music folder 
 Subsonic / Navidrome A server account 
 Internet Radio Nothing (30k+ stations from radio-browser.info) 
 YouTube yt-dlp on your PATH 
 Qobuz A paid Qobuz account 
 Apple Music macOS and the Music app 

Local Files, Subsonic, Internet Radio, YouTube and Qobuz play through spotatui's own audio engine. Apple Music plays in the Music app, and spotatui is its remote. The setup of each source is in Configuration.

Spotify plays in spotatui itself, on any Spotify Connect device, or on Cast and Connect speakers on your network. See Where Spotify plays. For lossless audio, or an account that native streaming cannot play, spotatui can run Spotify's own player: see Soloist.

 Learn more

 You want to Read 
 --- --- 
 Install another way, or build from source Installation 
 Change settings, keys or the theme Configuration, Keybindings, Themes 
 Control spotatui from your shell CLI 
 Write or install a Lua plugin PLUGINS.md, Scripting API 
 Let an AI pick the music AI DJ, MCP setup 
 Report a bug New issue, with a spotatui --debug log 
 Everything else All docs 

 Contributing

spotatui is built by a small team and a growing group of contributors, and you do not need to write code to help. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md, or pick a good first issue.

Native playback and Spotify Connect run on our librespot fork, spotatui-librespot. It is part of the project: a merged PR there counts as a spotatui contribution. See Contributing to the librespot fork.

 Code signing policy

Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.

The Windows release files are built from this repository by the release workflow on GitHub-hosted runners. Each signing request is approved by hand.

- Committers and reviewers: LargeModGames, ThatModGames, shilicioo, 2570165831, Oud
- Approvers: LargeModGames

Privacy: see the privacy policy for the data spotatui sends and how to turn each part off.

Everyone who helped, with code or without. To get on this list, see Recognition.
